coachingPoints: The pause is tiny — a beat, not a stop. A full stop lets the defender reset.
Keep the ball alive and low during the fake; a dead ball kills the advantage you just created.
Sell the slowdown with your whole body: sink, lean, exhale — then explode.
Change direction slightly on the burst; a straight-line hesitation is easier to recover on.
Read the defender's feet: if he stutters, backpedals, or hops, the hesitation worked — go.
commonMistakes: Picking up the dribble on the fake — fix: the hesitation only works because the ball is still live; keep dribbling through it.
Pausing too long — fix: count 'one' silently; if you reach 'two,' you waited too long.
Not actually slowing down — fix: exaggerate the pace drop in practice so the game-speed version reads clearly.
Hesitating with no plan — fix: decide your attack (drive or pull-up) before you start; the hesitation creates the moment, not the decision.
description: Slow down for a heartbeat to freeze the defender, then explode — the simplest and most effective change-of-pace move in basketball.
gameSituations: Attacking in transition — a hesitation on a 1-on-1 fast break can freeze the lone defender just long enough to blow past.
Setting up a pull-up — hesitate to make the defender relax, then rise for the jumper while he is still decelerating.
Against a fast, athletic defender — quick defenders reach early; a hesitation punishes their aggressiveness and turns their speed against them.

howTo.detail: Dribble toward the defender at a strong pace with your eyes up. The hesitation only works if he is playing you at speed first.
howTo.title: Attack at full speed

howTo.detail: Sink your hips, slow your dribble, and let your body drop for a beat. Everything — shoulders, ball, stride — says you are stopping.
howTo.title: Brake hard for one beat

howTo.detail: Lift your eyes as if looking for a pass or surveying the floor. This single cue convinces the defender the drive is over.
howTo.title: Sell the stop with your eyes

howTo.detail: Watch his reaction: a stutter step, a hop backward, or a hand dropped to the ball. Any freeze is your green light.
howTo.title: Read the defender's freeze

howTo.detail: Push off your outside foot and attack the lane or pull up — the burst must be maximum effort because the window lasts about half a second.
howTo.title: Explode past the freeze

title: Hesitation Move
whatIsIt: The hesitation is a change-of-pace move: you are attacking at speed, then suddenly slow down for a split second — like a driver tapping the brakes — before exploding again. The brief slowdown tricks the defender into relaxing or stopping, and you accelerate while he is flat-footed.

It is the quietest great move in basketball. There is no fancy ball trick; the ball stays in the same hand. The weapon is rhythm: you break the defender's timing, and broken timing becomes broken defense.
whyItMatters: Speed alone is easy to guard — defenders just backpedal. Pace changes are much harder, because the defender has to read and react to a false stop. The hesitation is the purest expression of this: one simple rhythm break that works at every level, from pickup games to the pros. Players who master it stop needing athleticism to beat defenders — timing does the work.
